[LERR.1.4.8] **Criterion.** No value — `null` included —
would be an honest answer ([LERR.1.4.1], [LERR.1.4.9]).
Answering `null` would say "unknown" when the truth is
"this computation is invalid", and would quietly turn a
rule bug into a rule that never fires. Silent continuation
would mean the engine reports progress that didn't happen.

Authors do not handle these as expression values — a trap
never feeds the `T?` / `??` / Kleene stack ([LCST.4.5.4]),
and the activation that raised it stays abandoned. A trap is
recorded on the stream ([RFCS.21]), and the engine then
asserts a `ComputationError` **fault fact** describing it
([LERR.9]), which a rule may match. The fact is a record of
the trap, never the value of the expression that raised it:
a rule reacts to *that* a computation failed, and still has
no answer to bind in its place.
